title: Get a hard pet carrier ready: slide the top to its click, lock both knobs, fit the door and close its four hinges
instruction: Get the pet carrier ready for use: top locked onto the bottom and the door fitted and shut.
context: About two thirds of US households keep a pet, and a hard carrier is what takes a cat or small dog to the vet; it is sold and stored as two nested shells and a loose door, and is taken apart again to be washed. Unlike a folding produce crate whose hinged walls swing up to corner catches, a picture-frame back held flush while its clips are turned, a power strip hung on keyhole studs and slid to lock (#2335), or a rabbit lifted into a carrier (#1596), here two separate shells are joined by a slide onto hooked tabs, locked by knobs that only turn once the slide is complete, and a loose door is captured by its four prongs in four twist hinges.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases (x forward, y to the robot's left), heights above the table. Carrier: a MidWest Spree 19 in plastic-door pet carrier, model 1419SPR-PD (published: 48 x 31.5 x 32 cm outside, 45.5 x 29.2 x 30.5 cm inside, doorway 18.2 x 19.4 cm, 0.97 kg), polypropylene, standing on its four feet with its door end toward the robot: front face at x 28, centred on y 0, back at x 76. Bottom shell (grey, 0.42 kg, loose on the table): rim 15.2 cm up with a 1.6 cm flange on each long side; a sill ledge 2.2 cm deep under the doorway with its top 6.7 cm up; a 3.8 cm knob on each front corner (centres at y +-13.5, 14 cm up), both unlocked (grip ridge upright); the two bottom door hinges at y +-8.6, open (levers pointing at the robot, 5 cm up). Top shell (red, 0.38 kg): resting on the bottom's rim at the back position, 1.1 cm behind home, its four hooked tabs standing in the four holes of the bottom's rim; its head ledge over the doorway is 27.3 to 27.7 cm up and carries the two top door hinges at y +-8.6, open (levers pointing at the robot, 28 cm up). Sliding the top forward takes about 3.7 N at the click (in the simulator a sprung ridge in each side rim stands in for the top's flexing tabs); each knob and each hinge turns a quarter turn against about 0.03 N m of friction. Door (light grey moulded grille, 19.4 x 20 x 1 cm, 0.12 kg, a 6 mm prong 2 cm long at each corner, 17.2 cm apart): standing upright, facing the robot, in the slot of a wooden stand (6 x 12 x 10 cm block, slot 1.1 cm wide and 3 cm deep, fixed to the table) centred at x 40, y 31, the door's bottom edge 7 cm up. The strap hooks are left off. Sizes other than the published ones are scaled from the photos in the assembly instructions.
scoring: End state; each level includes the ones before it. No level counts while a gripper is within 3 cm of the carrier or the door: every level needs both grippers at least 3 cm clear of them. Each level is given twice: what the simulator measures (millimetres and degrees, read from the model) and the check a person makes on the real carrier, whose top clicks home on flexing tabs; the simulator's sprung click ridges stand in for those tabs and are not looked for on the real carrier. 0.25, top clicked home. Simulator: no more than 1 mm behind its forward stop, less than 2.5 mm off to either side, the gap under its rim below 1.5 mm at all four corners, both click ridges back within 0.6 mm of their free height. Real trial: by eye, the top's front face is flush with the bottom's (a ruler laid across both shows no step over 1 mm), its sides are within 2.5 mm of the bottom's (ruler), and the rims meet all round (a 1.5 mm feeler gauge enters at none of the four corners); by a gentle test, a 2 N pull back on the top's front ledge (spring scale) does not move it, and lifting the top a little by its carry handle lifts the whole carrier, because the tabs are under the bottom's rim. 0.5, both knobs locked. Simulator: each turned at least 80 of its 90 degrees, its cam bar up behind the top's front wall. Real trial: each knob's grip ridge, upright when unlocked, lies within 10 degrees of level, and a gentle further turn clockwise does not move it (it is at its stop). 0.75, door fitted and shut. Simulator: each of the four prongs within 4.5 mm of its hinge's axis (a prong in a closed hinge cannot be more than 3.9 mm off it), the door within 5 mm of its seat on the sill, all four hinges turned at least 80 of their 90 degrees to closed. Real trial: by eye, each hinge lever is turned to closed (within 10 degrees of pointing at the middle of the door) with the door's corner prong inside it, and the door's bottom edge is within 5 mm of the sill; by a gentle test, a 2 N outward pull at each corner of the door (spring scale hooked through the grille) brings no corner out. 1.0: the 0.75 state held still. Simulator: no point of the carrier, the top or the door moves more than 1 mm in the last second. Real trial: no part visibly moves in the last second of the video, and pencil marks drawn across the top-to-bottom seam and at each corner of the door line up in the first and last frames of that second. Sliding or turning the carrier on the table costs nothing. 0 for good if the bottom shell was ever tipped more than 45 degrees (onto a side or an end), or the bottom shell, the top or the door ever left the table (video).
reset_notes: Turn all four door hinges to open (levers pointing out of the front) and take the door out; stand it in the stand's slot, facing the robot, the same way up. Turn both knobs back to unlocked (grip ridge upright). Slide the top back until its tabs stop at the back of their holes (1.1 cm), leaving it resting on the bottom's rim. Put the bottom shell back on its outline on the table.
fidelity: Rigid boxes at real size: straight 4 mm walls stand in for the tapered, ribbed shells; each door sunburst is 12 bars. The real top clicks home on flexing tabs; here a sprung ridge in each side rim gives the click (an estimated 3.7 N) at the same 11 mm slide, so the real checks (flush fronts, no rim gap, a 2 N pull that does not move the top) read the end state the simulator measures. Knob and hinge detents are friction. Unpublished sizes are scaled from the maker's photos; strap hooks left out.
